subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop propagating incompatible host dependency overrides into third-party managed plugin roots, or keep plugin packages fully responsible and only validate/report the mismatch?
rationale: The code path is compatibility and supply-chain sensitive: root overrides are used as OpenClaw security policy, but applying them into plugin-owned dependency graphs can break valid third-party packages.

options.title: Scope Managed-Root Overrides
options.body: Exclude or scope host overrides that conflict with plugin-owned dependency ranges, then prove Express 4 plugins keep `path-to-regexp` 0.1.x while OpenClaw core keeps 8.x.

options.title: Add Validator-Only Failure
options.body: Keep current override propagation but detect Express 4 plus incompatible `path-to-regexp` at install/update time and fail with an actionable package/shrinkwrap fix.

options.title: Document Plugin-Owned Pins
options.body: Keep the current behavior and document that affected plugins must publish their own shrinkwrap or override for Express 4 compatibility.

recommendation.title: Scope Managed-Root Overrides
recommendation.body: Exclude or scope host overrides that conflict with plugin-owned dependency ranges, then prove Express 4 plugins keep `path-to-regexp` 0.1.x while OpenClaw core keeps 8.x.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to the isolated plugin install architecture and dependency ownership docs that frame the policy choice.
